system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / for internal use. The Seller's documents have been reviewed as the counterparty's draft, not as agreed positions. Note at the outset that the Seller's cover note describes several points as "agreed" or "settled" (funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics"; Tax/IP "settled"). Nothing in our record supports that. We should state in our response that no position is agreed until documented in a signed term sheet or the executed SPA.

---

## 1. Departures from Playbook – Issue by Issue

### 1.1 General Warranty cap (Seller cl. 12.1) – 20% / AUD 4,800,000
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. **No such authority has been given.**
**Analysis:** The Seller has opened at exactly our fallback. We must not treat that as a meeting point. Respond with 25% / AUD 6,000,000. If the team wants to consider moving, that is an Amelia Frost decision and must be documented against this specific draft before any concession is communicated.
**Push back:** Yes – restore 25%.

### 1.2 Thresholds (Seller cl. 12.2) – de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once the basket is exceeded.
**Analysis:** Three separate departures: (a) de minimis is 5x ours; (b) basket is 5x ours; (c) "excess only" (deductible) rather than tipping basket. The deductible structure alone shifts AUD 250,000 of risk to us before any pro-rata effect. Combined with the high de minimis, a run of mid-sized claims (e.g. several AUD 20,000 items) would be entirely irrecoverable.
**Push back:** Yes on all three. Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping (first dollar).

### 1.3 General claims period (Seller cl. 12.3/13) – 18 months
**Playbook:** 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval – **none given**.
**Analysis:** Same pattern as the cap: the Seller has opened at our fallback. Revert to 24 months. A 24-month window also covers two audit cycles post-Completion, which matters for accounts-based warranties.
**Push back:** Yes – 24 months.

### 1.4 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (Seller cl. 12.3/13) and "limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature" (Seller cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5)
**Playbook:** Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override. Fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
**Analysis:** This is the most structurally dangerous part of the Seller's package and it is dressed as drafting convenience. Read together, these provisions would:
- Pull Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP and specific indemnity claims (including Ironquay) into the 20% cap, AUD 250,000 deductible and 18-month window.
- Apply exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to **fraud**. A non-reliance/exclusive-remedy clause purporting to cover fraudulent misrepresentation is of doubtful enforceability under NSW law and the Australian Consumer Law in any event, but we should not rely on a court to fix it – the carve-out must be express.
- Reverse the default: anything not expressly carved out is caught. We want the opposite default.
**Push back:** Yes – delete both "all Claims" formulations. Insert an express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from every limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provision "to the maximum extent permitted by law", and an express statement that specific indemnities, Tax, IP, Title/Fundamental and covenant claims sit outside Clause 12 except where a specific provision says otherwise. **Non-negotiable per playbook.**

### 1.5 Fundamental / Title warranties subject to general caps and time limits
**Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% cap, at least six years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
**Analysis:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title. If the Seller does not own, or cannot transfer, unencumbered title to 100% of the shares, our loss is the full price, not 20% of it. An 18-month limit is also inconsistent with the six-year limitation period for contract claims in NSW and with the latency of title defects (often surfacing on a later exit).
**Push back:** Yes – separate Fundamental/Title regime at 100% of price, six years minimum, no basket/de minimis, no knowledge qualifier.

### 1.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter [1.1], [1.2])
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Analysis:** [1.1] deems the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) disclosed; [1.2] adds Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". This is precisely the general disclosure the playbook rejects. The effect is that any warranty could be defeated by pointing to a document buried in the data room, regardless of whether it was fairly brought to our attention. Note also [1.4] – the non-admission paragraph – which is acceptable in itself but, combined with general disclosure, lets the Seller disclose a problem without characterising it and then say we were on notice.
**Push back:** Yes – delete [1.1] and [1.2] as general disclosures. Require that only matters fairly disclosed in the specific paragraphs of the Disclosure Letter, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter, qualify the warranties. The data room index may be annexed for reference but must not be deemed disclosed.

### 1.7 Buyer knowledge exclusion (Seller cl. 8.3)
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
**Analysis:** Cl. 8.3 excludes any matter of which "the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." This is three problems in one: (a) actual knowledge of the Buyer; (b) imputed knowledge of advisers; (c) **constructive** knowledge – anything "discoverable". Paired with 1.6, it converts warranties into something close to a nullity. It would also bar title and fraud claims on the Seller's "all Claims" drafting.
**Push back:** Yes – delete cl. 8.3 entirely. If the Seller insists on a knowledge concept, it should be a *Seller* knowledge qualifier on specified warranties only, defined by reference to named individuals (e.g. the Paperbark CEO, CFO, CTO) after due and careful enquiry. Never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 1.8 Bluefen consent (Seller cl. 3/6.3; Disclosure Letter para 2)
**Playbook:** Effective consent AND evidence its conditions (DD-002 cl. 11.3) are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient.
**Analysis:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3,600,000 / ~30% of FY26 revenue – the single largest customer. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms **no** final written consent and **no** evidence that cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied. The proposed mechanic ("satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent") means a conditional or qualified consent letter satisfies the CP even if the conditions are never met. "Reasonable endeavours" is the weakest endeavours standard.
**Push back:** Yes. Condition Precedent must be: (i) unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl. 11.2, in agreed form; (ii) written evidence satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably) that each cl. 11.3 condition has been satisfied or waived by Bluefen; (iii) no notice of termination, re-pricing or material variation. Seller obligation: all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours, with Buyer right to participate in discussions. Consider a Bluefen-specific warranty and price protection (retention or earn-out adjustment) if consent is delayed.

### 1.9 Riverlark facility (Seller cl. 2/7; Disclosure Letter para 3)
**Playbook:** Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
**Analysis:** ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, with a change-of-control trigger (cl. 8.1) and security over the Company. The Seller proposes a release "following Completion" – i.e. we would complete with the bank's security in place and a change-of-control event already triggered. This is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal and exposes the Company (now ours) to acceleration.
**Push back:** Yes. Require: (i) Riverlark payout letter dated no more than 2 business days before Completion; (ii) repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow; (iii) executed releases/discharges of all security (PPSR, any real property, share mortgages, guarantees) delivered at Completion, with PPSR deregistration undertaken within an agreed period. A post-completion release should only be entertained if the bank gives an irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt of funds – and that requires Amelia Frost's approval, which should be sought before we signal any flexibility.

### 1.10 Employee bonuses – DD-005 AUD 420,000 (Funds flow; Disclosure Letter para 5)
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Analysis:** The Seller's parenthetical – "a matter for the Seller and not separately itemised" – is contradictory. If it is a matter for the Seller, it should appear as a Seller-funded line item. If it is not itemised, in practice the Company (post-Completion, ours) pays it. The Disclosure Letter is also silent on superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs, which on AUD 420,000 could add a material amount. Bonuses triggered by Completion are a classic Transaction Cost / Debt-like item in a debt-free/cash-free deal.
**Push back:** Yes. Either (a) specific funds-flow line: AUD 420,000 plus all on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, leave accruals affected) paid by Seller or deducted from the price; or (b) treated as Debt/Transaction Expenses in the completion accounts. Obtain a Seller warranty that DD-005 is a complete list of Completion-triggered payments.

### 1.11 Ironquay IP (Seller cl. 11.1; Disclosure Letter para 4)
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
**Analysis:** DD-004 cl. 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; the Seller correctly flags this is not bank-verified, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment – not the loss if IP ownership fails, not third-party claims, not the cost of re-procuring or replacing the materials, and not other SOWs that may have similar conditions.
**Push back:** Yes. Preferred route is a **cure** – Seller pays the AUD 180,000 (or whatever is verified outstanding) pre-Completion and delivers Ironquay's written acknowledgement of payment and a confirmatory IP assignment as a Completion deliverable. In addition, broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have clear title to Ironquay-developed materials (all SOWs), on a pound-for-pound basis, outside the general cap/basket/time limit. Request bank evidence of payment status from the Seller – we should not assume either payment or non-payment.

### 1.12 Export/privacy incident – DD-006 (Seller cl. 4.6/Sch. 6; Disclosure Letter para 6)
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
**Analysis:** The Seller characterises this as "preliminary operational" and "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter is more candid: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address, access and scope unknown, notification requirement undetermined, investigation preliminary. We should neither accept the Seller's "not material" label nor over-characterise it as a breach. The real issue is that the facts are not yet known and the Seller is proposing to disclose it generally (see 1.6) so that any later consequence is excluded.
**Push back:** Yes, as process rather than price at this stage. Require: (i) a pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs, email records and link-access data; (ii) completion of the investigation (including whether the link was accessed, and by whom) and a written report to the Buyer before Completion; (iii) an obligation to update the Disclosure Letter at Completion; (iv) a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification, third-party claims), outside the general regime, so that the general disclosure does not neutralise the privacy warranties. We make no assumption that notification is required or that any loss has crystallised.

### 1.13 Sandbar renewals – AUD 330,000 (Disclosure Letter para 8)
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Analysis:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each. The Seller calls them ordinary-course operating costs; the Disclosure Letter admits it does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We should not reflexively demand a price reduction, but we need the facts.
**Push back:** Request DD-008 and DD-011 be read together with an explanation of: timing of commitment, whether any was accelerated or pre-paid, whether they are reflected in the Accounts/working capital, and whether they were entered or renewed in the period between Accounts Date and Completion (which engages the pre-Completion conduct covenants). If they are genuinely recurring operating costs in the normal cycle, they stay in working capital. If any were brought forward or are outside the normal cycle, treat as a Leakage / Debt-like item.

### 1.14 Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"
**Playbook:** Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
**Analysis:** Not settled. The Seller is attempting to lock Tax and IP into the 20% cap / AUD 250,000 deductible / 18-month window by assertion. Tax warranties and a tax indemnity typically run to the relevant statutory limitation/amendment periods; IP warranties for a software analytics business are fundamental to value.
**Push back:** Record expressly that Tax and IP are open. Our position is a separate regime for each (we are not asserting unlimited liability – terms to be agreed), outside the general cap, basket and 18/24-month window.

### 1.15 Title – evidenced by DD-012 share register
**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
**Analysis:** The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 10) concedes DD-012 is the source "relied on" and that it does not state the Buyer has verified it. A company's own register is Seller-controlled. It does not show share mortgages, PPSR registrations over shares, ASIC-recorded members, or the Seller's own corporate authority.
**Push back:** Require as Completion deliverables / our own DD: ASIC company extract and historical member search; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller; Seller board resolution and (if required) shareholder approval; constitution check for pre-emptive rights/transfer restrictions; executed transfer, share certificates (or evidence of cancellation), and Riverlark release of any share security (links to 1.9). Title warranty remains on the Fundamental regime (1.5).

### 1.16 Other Disclosure Letter items (not material departures, but note)
- **Office lease (para 7):** notification only, not landlord consent. Acceptable; add a pre-Completion covenant to give the notification and deliver a copy.
- **Mossvale (para 9):** restriction on assignment, not a change-of-control consent. Acceptable on its face; confirm the clause does not contain an indirect change-of-control trigger.
- **Para [1.4] non-admission and para 11 reservation:** acceptable as drafting, but they reinforce why we need specific disclosure – the Seller is disclosing facts without characterising them and leaving us to draw conclusions.

---

## 2. Pattern Observations

1. **The Seller has opened at our fallbacks on cap and claims period.** This is either coincidence or a leak. Either way, we must not negotiate from those figures; neither has been authorised by Amelia Frost and both require her written approval referencing this draft.
2. **The "all Claims" drafting is the lynchpin.** Several individually tolerable-sounding clauses (12.3, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5, Fundamental folded into general) combine to produce a single 20% / 18-month / AUD 250,000-deductible regime for everything including title and fraud, defeated further by general disclosure and constructive buyer knowledge. Our response should treat these as one package and reject it as a package.
3. **Three Completion-critical items are unresolved on the Seller's own admission:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay SOW3. None can be left to "reasonable endeavours" or "following Completion".
4. **The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the cover note.** Use it: the Seller's own paragraphs 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10 confirm the gaps we are relying on.

---

## 3. Summary of Recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m.** 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority – none given. |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k de minimis / AUD 250k deductible basket | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping basket**, first-dollar recovery. |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | **24 months.** 18 only with Amelia Frost written approval – none given. |
| 4 | "All Claims" limitation / exclusive remedy / non-reliance | Applies to everything | **Delete.** Express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from all limits; express exclusion of Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenant claims from the general regime. Non-negotiable. |
| 5 | Fundamental / Title | Same as general | **Separate regime:** 100% cap, 6 years minimum, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar. |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | **Specific fair disclosure only.** Delete DL [1.1] and [1.2] as general disclosure. |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3) | Blanket, incl. advisers and "discoverable" matters | **Delete.** Any knowledge concept = Seller knowledge, named persons, reasonable enquiry; never for title/capacity/fraud/indemnities. |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **CP: unconditional consent + evidence cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied, pre-Completion.** Best/all reasonable endeavours; Buyer participation; consider retention. |
| 9 | Riverlark | Release post-Completion | **Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion.** Post-completion release only with irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval. |
| 10 | DD-005 bonuses | Not itemised; "matter for Seller" | **Specific funds-flow line, Seller-funded, including superannuation/payroll tax/on-costs.** Warranty that DD-005 is complete. |
| 11 | Ironquay | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | **Cure pre-Completion** (payment + Ironquay acknowledgement + confirmatory assignment) **plus broadened IP ownership indemnity** outside general regime. Verify AUD 180k via bank evidence – not assumed either way. |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Log preservation, completed investigation and report pre-Completion, DL update at Completion, specific indemnity.** No assumption of breach, harm, notification duty or quantum. |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Assess.** Request timing/scope detail; working capital if genuinely recurring, Leakage/Debt-like if accelerated. No automatic deduction. |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | **Open.** Separate regimes to be negotiated; not within general cap/basket/period. No unlimited liability asserted. |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence:** ASIC extract, PPSR, constitution, Seller authorities, Riverlark share-security release. |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only / assignment restriction | Acceptable; add notification covenant; confirm no indirect CoC trigger in Mossvale. |

**Immediate actions:**
1. Confirm to the Seller in writing that no positions are agreed or settled and that our mark-up follows.
2. Brief Amelia Frost that the Seller has opened at our cap and period fallbacks; obtain her instruction (expected: hold at 25% / 24 months) before any communication on those points.
3. Issue supplementary DD requests: Bluefen consent correspondence, Riverlark payout letter, Ironquay bank evidence, DD-005 on-cost calculation, DD-006 investigation status and log preservation confirmation, Sandbar DD-008/DD-011 timing, ASIC/PPSR title searches.
4. Prepare the SPA mark-up with the structural fix (item 4) as the lead point, since most other protections depend on it.
=== END ADVICE ===
